styleRules: Register: 你, never 您. A 您 anywhere is a defect.
No em dash (U+2014) and no en dash (U+2013), including the Chinese 破折号 '——'. Restructure with ，、：；。or （）.
Full-width Chinese punctuation in Chinese sentences; half-width only inside complete English sentences, code, and proper nouns. Digits always half-width.

Pangu spacing: one space between CJK and Latin letters, digits, or product names (Phi 的、16 GB 内存、使用 Bitwarden). No space between a digit and its unit when the unit is a CJK character (3 个). No space next to full-width punctuation.
Corner quotes 「」 for quoted UI labels and short quotations; 『』 for nesting. Never use "" or “” in Chinese prose.
Enumerations use 、. If / is unavoidable, one space on each side.
Menu paths keep the arrow and bold: **设置 → 开发者 → 智能体控制**.
UI labels in bold reproduce the shipped zh-Hans product label when one exists; otherwise translate naturally and flag as unverified.
No exclamation-mark inflation: at most what the English uses, usually none.
No trailing period on labels, buttons, table cells that are labels, or nav entries.
Keyboard symbols (⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ⌃ ⌫ ↩) and key names stay as in the English source.
Voice: a capable colleague explaining at a desk. Direct, honest about limits, no hype, no 请注意 or 值得一提的是 padding, no 简单地 / 只需 / 轻松 (the Chinese equivalents of simply / just / easy).
Never add product claims, never soften a stated limitation, never turn a future or conditional statement into present tense.
